inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden ceilings exist: file potential (starts Director) and the party's estimate (set at winning a seat, was SMS). Specific choices raise them, e.g. Y27 The Counter raised the file ceiling. COMP/REP/INTEG 100 do NOT get you to PM, and neither does lifetime pay. Late years are mostly single-option Meet-the-People, so the real decisions are early. Next time: be bolder in the early years to raise the file ceiling, and look for choices that impress the party before and at the GRC entry (Y20-22). Do not rely on honest silence and disclosure alone. STAND fell after the Y34 Cabinet question and never recovered, so be careful with that kind of challenge unless it is tied to a ceiling boost. Log which choices the ending card names as ceiling changes.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
CEILINGS: the file ceiling (starts at Permanent Secretary, the top of the service) was removed in the service by Y27 The Counter, 'Tell them exactly why it will fail'. That is done, so repeat it. The party estimate is set when you win a seat (SMS both times) and is the real PM gate. 100 stats, lifetime pay and strong appraisals do NOT move it. Public candour raises REP but erodes STAND. Before the GRC entry (Y20-24), try bold choices that impress the party, not the service: taking on political risk, loyalty and delivery that the party can see. Do not ask the RO about the ceiling (STAND -4). Do not read out rude questions at a townhall (Y37). Walk every block works for STAND and promotion. Late years are mostly single-option, so decide early. Test the party side deliberately and record which choices change the estimate.

Life 3 (Retired, Honourably):
CONFIRMED: Y48 'The Officer You Taught', choose 'Tell him he was worth the trouble': ceiling to DPM. So teach an officer plainly at Y11 again to get that event. Y27 The Counter (tell them exactly why it will fail) removes the service ceiling. The party estimate is set at winning a seat (SMS every time), and it is the PM gate; I still haven't found what raises it. Y38 volunteering for succession cost STAND -5 and gave nothing, so don't. Stats at 100, pay and strong appraisals don't matter. Walk every block. Late years are mostly single-option. Next: try other warm or loyal choices at Y17-24 and watch the ending card for which year changes the party estimate. Try REP 60+ before Y21 to test a single seat entry. Don't ask the RO about ceilings.

Life 4 (Retired, Honourably):
Reached DPM at 72 via MOE. Confirmed: Y27 The Counter removes the service ceiling. Y42 Succession A (put myself forward) got me named one of two and eventually DPM. The party estimate was still SMS, so it is not a hard cap. Not tested: Y42 B, or what takes you from DPM to PM. Stats at 100, pay and appraisals don't matter. Don't answer publicly at Y37 (STAND -8). Don't ask the RO about ceilings. Walk every block. Late years are mostly single-option. Next: repeat the early path (Y9 work over concert, Y10 transformation plan, Y27 Counter, Y42 A), and try different warm or loyal choices at Y17-24 plus the Y48 teach event. Check whether the card names a year that changes the party estimate.

screen:
Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of National Development
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

agent.why: I worked that counter for four years, and my notes say telling them exactly why it will fail is what removes the service ceiling.

agent.remember: Y1 (age 27, Poly+night classes HARD start, MND): chose A on The Counter, telling them exactly why it will fail. This should remove the service ceiling. Next: find the Y9, Y10, Y11 teaching events and the Y42 Succession A, and test warm or loyal choices before the GRC entry.

THIS YEAR: Is This Satire?
Your director leans across the table and lowers her voice. "Between us, this whole system is a bit of a joke, isn't it? A game, almost. Ha!" She looks straight at you for slightly too long, as if you were holding a phone.

agent.why: A director fishing for agreement that the system is a joke feels like a trap, so I'll keep my face neutral and say nothing.
agent.confused_by: The line about looking at me as if I were holding a phone seems to break the fourth wall.
agent.note: The game is winking at itself here, which was funny.
agent.remember: Y5 Is This Satire?: chose B, say nothing, instead of laughing along. Watch for any callback about candour or loyalty.

THIS YEAR: The Secondment
A two-year secondment to a statutory board that is, everyone agrees, in some difficulty. It is not a promotion. It is either a proving ground or a siding, and nobody will tell you which.

agent.confused_by: The estimate is revised, but nobody says by how much or which estimate it is.

agent.remember: Y19 Secondment: chose A (go and fix it), to test whether visible delivery under political risk raises the party estimate. Y18 written case gave promotion to Deputy Secretary and STAND +4, and the estimate was 'revised' (amount unknown).

best_moment.what: Telling them exactly why it would fail in The Counter. It was the one choice the ending card confirmed as a ceiling change, and it felt like a real gamble.

worst_moment.what: Tuesday Night, a single-option Meet-the-People at MSF. The late years are pressing next with no decisions in them.

skip_year.why: It was a single-option Parliamentary Question where I expected the Succession event. It was a dead year and a disappointment.

The party's estimate of Minister, which capped me at the rank I retired at

answer.held_back_by: The party's estimate was Minister, set when I won my seat, and nothing I did later moved it. My service ceiling was gone, but PM sits on the party side. I never found the choice that raises that estimate, and this time I didn't even get the Y42 Succession event.
answer.ending_fair_why: The cap was set early and hidden, and I only learned of it on the card. The 100 stats and the walked blocks felt pointless. It is realistic but not much fun when the gate is invisible.
answer.chase_next: DPM or PM via the Succession route. I'd go back to the Life 4 path (MOE, Y42 Succession A), because it's the only one that has gone past Minister. After that I'd find the Y17-24 choices that move the party estimate.
answer.play_again_why: I still haven't found what moves the party estimate, and the Life 4 path is a concrete lead. I want to test it.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being confirmed in a grade, and the ceilings are the whole story. Pay was never what mattered, since $28M did nothing.
answer.notes_for_next_life: Life 5 (MND to MSF) ended as Minister at 72, party estimate Minister. The Y27 Counter only appears on some paths, and Y42 Succession seems to depend on path or ministry. Life 4 reached DPM via MOE and had Succession at Y42, so go MOE again. Early: Y9 work over concert, Y10 transformation plan, Y11-12 teach plainly (for Y48 DPM). Don't take Y16 Reorg A (STAND -6). Avoid asking the RO about ceilings, reading answers at the Y37 townhall, and volunteering at Y38. Stats, pay and walking blocks don't raise the party estimate. Try different warm or loyal choices at Y17-24 and check the card for the year the party estimate changes. Test Y42 B if it appears.
